Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 2
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a critical logical error by misinterpreting the role of Nelson Rockefeller. The WebSurfer correctly identified that Alfred Balk served as secretary to "New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller's Committee." However, the Planner incorrectly inferred that because Nelson Rockefeller was involved, he must be the "United States Vice President" in question. This is a factual error: Nelson Rockefeller was the Governor of New York at the time of the committee's existence, not the Vice President. The Planner failed to distinguish between Rockefeller's state-level role (Governor) and federal roles (Vice President), leading to the selection of Spiro Agnew (who was VP under Nixon) instead of the correct answer, Nelson Rockefeller (who served as VP under Gerald Ford). The error stems from conflating the name "Nelson Rockefeller" with the specific title "Vice President" without verifying the timeline or the specific capacity in which he held the title relative to the committee.
